correctness.rationale: The outside complement W=F\U of any owner-effective event U⊇St(v) must meet each external b-colored witness star St(v_b(X))\St(v); this is a direct equivalence to Wang’s SN clause at every owner facet X. In a two-agent simple bipartite graph the neighbor-specific witness sets D_b consist of edges (u,b) with u≠v, are pairwise disjoint, each with d(b)−1 elements; free edges contribute 2^{|E|−Σ_b d(b)}. For three agents, a full B×C owner v-star and w-facets indexed by bipartite H mean selecting the outside w-facets is precisely selecting an edge cover meeting every vertex of B and C, including isolated-vertex zero counts. This parsimonious reduction and the cited known #Bipartite-Edge-Cover hardness establish #P hardness; explicit facet enumeration establishes #P membership. Globally shared added-color vertices do not change this witness requirement since nonempty covers are already forced. Independently enumerated K_{2,2} edge covers=7 and a 2-agent 2×2 model event count=1. The proof is conditional on semantic SN and arbitrary potential event truth sets, not fixed-valuation definability.
